style.vernacular: Equatorial Atlantic capital with a tropical monsoon climate (about 2,800 mm of rain a year, 83% humidity): French-colonial and 1970s oil-boom concrete blocks of 2-5 storeys in weathered cream, pale grey and pastel painted render with rain-streaked, mould-darkened walls, older timber and plank houses with verandas in the neighbourhoods, dense hillside quarters of single-storey block houses under rusty corrugated roofs, wide seafront boulevards, red-brown laterite soil and lush palm and broadleaf growth.
style.ornament: Colonial-era timber verandas and louvred shutters on older houses; 1970s-80s monumental modernist civic blocks with brise-soleil, concrete grilles and flag courts built after the 1977 OAU summit; weathered mildew streaking on every concrete surface; hand-painted shop signs and murals in market districts.

sources.what: tropical monsoon climate (rainfall ~2,840 mm, humidity ~83%), 1977 OAU-summit prestige building wave, Mont-Bouet market, Baie des Rois waterfront redevelopment
